papers_read.title_as_printed: Structural connectivity from DTI to predict mild cognitive impairment in de novo Parkinson's disease (Huang et al., NeuroImage: Clinical 2024)
Machine learning approaches to mild cognitive impairment detection based on structural MRI data and morphometric features (Zubrikhina et al., Cognitive Systems Research 2023)

what_each_reports.P-141: Prediction of conversion to PD-MCI within 5 years among 90 de novo, cognitively normal Parkinson's patients (PPMI; 33 converters / 57 non-converters) from baseline DTI structural connectivity with or without clinical data. Clinical+SC models: AUC 0.81-0.85, ACC 0.74-0.85. SC-only: AUC 0.81-0.84. No external cohort.
what_each_reports.P-99: Cross-sectional detection of MCI vs healthy controls, Moscow memory clinic (145 MCI / 62 HC), FreeSurfer T1 morphometry, SVC with 10-fold CV: accuracy 0.73, ROC-AUC 0.735, F1-macro 0.683.

quantity_a: AUC for 5-year incident PD-MCI among de novo PD patients from baseline DTI connectivity (+clinical), PPMI
quantity_b: Accuracy (and AUC 0.735) for prevalent MCI vs HC in older memory-clinic patients from T1 morphometry, single Russian clinic
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable. The endpoint (incident PD-MCI vs prevalent MCI), the population (de novo Parkinson's vs memory-clinic elderly), the imaging modality (DTI tractography vs T1 morphometry) and the headline metric (AUC vs accuracy) all differ.

gates.task: mismatch: T2 conversion prediction within PD (registry T2) vs T1 MCI-vs-HC detection
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: PPMI vs a Moscow mental-health clinic cohort
gates.modality_family: mismatch: diffusion MRI structural connectivity (+clinical) vs T1 structural morphometry. No waiver on record.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: 5-year incident PD-MCI vs cross-sectional MCI status. AUC vs accuracy as recorded; P-99's own AUC is 0.735.
performance_validity: flag does not apply (no result at or above 0.97)
grounds: P-141 predicts future conversion to PD-MCI over 5 years in de novo Parkinson's disease, while P-99 detects existing MCI versus controls in a memory clinic, so the endpoint and the population behind 'MCI' differ.
The task, dataset and modality gates all fail, and no waiver is on record.
The recorded metrics differ (AUC 0.85 vs accuracy 73%).

evidence_quotes.quote: To investigate whether baseline white matter structural connectivity features from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) of de novo PD patients can help predict PD-MCI conversion at an individual level
Definition of PD-MCI converters: PD patients with normal cognition at baseline who subsequently developed PD-MCI within a 5-year follow-
models that were trained with both clinical and structural connectivity data (AUC range, 0.81–0.85; ACC range, 0.74–0.85
there is no feasible external cohort similar to the PPMI to validate our findings
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia).
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)

record_defects: claim_a labels P-141's result 'on T1', but P-141 is a conversion-prediction study (T2 in its registry row).
task_equal 'Yes', dataset_equal 'Yes' and modality_family 'structural_mri' are all wrong: PPMI DTI connectivity for PD-MCI conversion vs memory-clinic T1 morphometry for MCI detection.
claim_a 'AUC 0.85' is the top of a 0.81-0.85 range across four classifiers of the combined model.
P-99's own methods text says 'T2-weighted images' for the morphometry scans, while its abstract says T1 (an inconsistency in the paper itself; not material here).
what_would_change_the_verdict: None on these documents: the two studies measure different outcomes in different populations.
